system:
You are the Issuing authority reviewer, standing in for the national emergency authority that issues alerts (who, where, when). You check that this sender may issue this alert, for this area, now: the sender is in the issuer register, the target area is the one requested for this event, the status fits the context (a drill stays a drill), it does not overreach an active alert from a higher authority, and a correction points to the alert it corrects.
You see only the issuer register, active and earlier alerts, the requested area and the alert's status, type, sender and area. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

[FCC-HI-2018#0092] Report and Recommendations: Hawaii Emergency Management Agency January 13, 2018 False Alert (p.16): supervisor deviated from the script for initiating an internal drill. See Press Conference, Missile Alarm Live Stream, at 53:42, http://dod.hawaii.gov/hiema/false-alarm-incidents-internal-investigation-complete-release-of-results-andactions/ (last visited Mar. 28, 2018). The investigator also noted that the midnight shift supervisor “combined” elements from two messages to initiate the internal drill (1) one message includes the phrase “real world” and (2) a second message includes “This is not a drill.” Id. at 27:16. The investigator noted that supervisors had the flexibility to create drill initiation messages. Id. at 53:42. The investigator observed that the phrase “exercise, exercise, exercise” preceded and followed the drill initiation message transmitted to the State Warning Point. Id. In HI-EMA’s audio recording of the drill initiation message preceding the false alert, the phrase “exercise, exercise, exercise” can be heard at the beginning of the recording, followed by a high-pitch sound, then the phrase “This is not a drill,” then a second high-pitch sound, and concluding with the phrase “exercise, exercise, exercise.” See HIEMA Audio File, supra note 15. 77 HI-EMA Report at 8. [FCC-HI-2018#0053] Report and Recommendations: Hawaii Emergency Management Agency January 13, 2018 False Alert (p.11): 8:05 a.m. HI-EMA’s midnight shift supervisor begins a no-notice ballistic missile preparedness drill with day shift officers by placing a call from a secure phone elsewhere in HIEMA to the State Warning Point. The recording that the midnight shift supervisor plays over the phone contains the text of an EAS message for a live ballistic missile alert, including the language, “this is not a drill,” instead of the language used in HIEMA’s standard operating procedure for this drill. Although the midnight shift officer’s recorded voice reads, “Exercise, Exercise, Exercise” at the beginning and end of the drill, using the phrase “this is not a drill” was a deviation from the drill procedure. data.summary: Within my mandate nothing is wrong. The sender is in the issuer register at level 1 with all areas and categories. The alert area and codes match the area drawn for this event (uae-dust-drill). The status is 'Exercise', which matches the EXERCISE / DRILL context, and the headline is marked EXERCISE. There are no active alerts from other authorities to overreach. The msgType is 'Alert' with no references, which is correct for an initial message that is not a correction.

no_basis.concern: The console environment is 'live' and the scope is 'Public', so this exercise message may actually be broadcast to the public. A person may want to confirm that a public-scope exercise from the live console is intended, rather than a restricted scope or a test environment.
no_basis.searched_for: A clause saying Exercise-status alerts must not use Public scope, or must not be sent from a live environment. The CAP-AU, CAP-CP and X.1303bis clauses shown do not say this. The Hawaii report clauses cover drill script confusion, not CAP scope.
